verses.text: This happened in the days of King Xerxes, also called Ahasuerus. He ruled over one hundred twenty-seven provinces, from India all the way to Ethiopia.
At that time King Xerxes ruled his kingdom from his royal throne in the fortress city of Susa.
In the third year of his rule, he gave a big feast for all his officials and servants. The army leaders of Persia and Media, the important men, and the governors of the provinces were there with him.
For a long time, one hundred eighty days, he showed off the great wealth of his kingdom and the glory and greatness of his royal power.

When those days were over, the king gave a seven-day feast for all the people in the fortress city of Susa, from the most important to the least. It was held in the garden courtyard of the king's palace.

There were curtains of white and blue cloth, tied with cords of fine white linen and purple material to silver rings on marble pillars. There were couches of gold and silver on a floor made of red, white, yellow, and black marble.
Drinks were served in gold cups, each one different from the others. There was plenty of royal wine, because the king was very generous.
By the king's order, no one was forced to drink. The king had told all the servants in his palace to give each guest whatever they wanted.
Queen Vashti also gave a feast for the women in King Xerxes' royal palace.
On the seventh day, when the king was in high spirits from the wine, he gave orders to the seven officials who served him: Mehuman, Biztha, Harbona, Bigtha, Abagtha, Zethar, and Carcas.
He told them to bring Queen Vashti to him wearing her royal crown, so he could show off her beauty to the people and the officials, because she was very beautiful.
But when the officials gave Queen Vashti the king's order, she refused to come. Then the king became very angry. His anger burned inside him.
The king spoke with the wise men who understood the times, because it was his custom to ask advice from experts in law and justice.

The men closest to him were Carshena, Shethar, Admatha, Tarshish, Meres, Marsena, and Memucan, the seven officials of Persia and Media. They could meet with the king at any time and had the highest positions in the kingdom.
The king asked, "What does the law say should be done to Queen Vashti? She did not obey King Xerxes' order that the officials brought to her."

Memucan answered in front of the king and the officials, "Queen Vashti has not only done wrong to the king. She has also done wrong to all the officials and all the people in all the provinces of King Xerxes.
All the women will hear what the queen did, and they will look down on their husbands. They will say, 'King Xerxes ordered Queen Vashti to be brought to him, but she would not come.'
This very day the important women of Persia and Media who have heard what the queen did will tell all the king's officials the same thing. There will be no end of disrespect and anger.

If it pleases the king, let him give a royal order and let it be written in the laws of Persia and Media, which cannot be changed. The order should say that Vashti may never again come into King Xerxes' presence. Let the king give her royal position to someone else who is better than she is.
When the king's order is announced all through his huge kingdom, all the wives will respect their husbands, from the most important to the least."
The king and his officials liked this advice, so the king did what Memucan said.

He sent letters to all the provinces of his kingdom, to each province in its own writing and to each people in their own language. The letters said that every man should be the ruler of his own home and should speak the language of his own people.
